text: To tout something is to praise it loudly and often so people will believe in it or buy it. Here, makers keep touting fancy powders as better.
Prolonged means lasting longer than usual. Here, the muscles kept building for a longer stretch of time.
Unadulterated means pure, with nothing else mixed in. Plain whey powder with no fillers is unadulterated.
Alchemists were people long ago who tried to turn ordinary metals like lead into gold. It never worked, which is why the writer jokes that turning waste into powder was the next best thing.
Whey is the thin, watery liquid left over when milk is turned into cheese. It holds a fast-acting kind of protein.
A gym rat is a person who spends a lot of time working out at the gym. It is a friendly nickname.
To pay top dollar means to pay a very high price, as much as anyone would pay.
Casein is the main protein in the solid part of milk, the curds that become cheese. Your body digests it slowly.
Leguminous plants are the bean and pea family. They grow their seeds in pods.
Leucine is one kind of amino acid. It helps tell your muscles to grow and also helps build them.
Amino acids are the small building blocks that proteins are made of. Think of them as beads on a necklace.
Usually essential means very important. Here it has a special meaning: an amino acid your body cannot make, so it has to come from food.
Synthesis means building something by putting smaller pieces together. Muscle synthesis is your body building new muscle from protein.
A biochemical pathway is a chain of tiny steps inside the body, each one passing a signal to the next, like dominoes falling.
mTOR is a switch inside your cells. When it turns on, the cells start building protein.
To replenish means to fill something up again after it has been used. After exercise, the body refills its muscles.
Muscle fibres are the thin, stretchy strands that make up a muscle. Exercise causes tiny wear in them, and the body fixes them.
A brick is the material and a bricklayer is the worker who builds with it. So leucine is both the material and the worker.
A kinesiologist is a scientist who studies how the body moves and how muscles work.
Brawn means strong muscles and physical strength.
Standard here means the usual size or kind, the one most people use.
A scoop is the measuring spoon that comes in the tub. One scoop is one serving.
The quadriceps are the big muscles on the front of your thigh, above the knee.
A participant is a person who takes part in a study or an activity.
Across the board means affecting everyone or everything, with no exceptions.
Curds are the thick lumps that form when milk is split. They get pressed into cheese.
Cheesemaking is the craft of turning milk into cheese. It splits milk into solid curds and liquid whey.
Soya is the British spelling of soy, a bean used to make tofu and soy milk.
A serving is the amount of food meant for one person. Per serving means in each of those portions.
Refined means cleaned up or processed more so that it is purer or finer.
An isolate is a version where almost everything else has been removed to leave mostly just the protein.
Lactose is the natural sugar in milk. Some people have trouble digesting it.
A hydrolysate is protein that has been broken into smaller pieces in advance, so it is easier to digest.
Enzymes are tiny helpers in living things that speed up chemical changes, such as breaking down food.
A concoction is a mixture made by combining several things, often a strange one.
A buff is a fan or expert about something. Gym buffs love working out.
Your best bet means the choice most likely to turn out well.
Leavened normally describes dough that rises with yeast. Here it means the powders have extra stuff mixed in.
Glycine is a cheap amino acid. It is not very helpful for building muscle.
Taurine is another cheap amino acid, also found in many energy drinks.
To inflate is to make something look bigger than it really is, like blowing up a balloon.
Emulsifiers are ingredients that keep oil and water mixed together so a food stays smooth.
Starches are cheap fillers made from plants like corn or potatoes.

forms: not all that glitters is muscle-building gold
text: The saying is: not all that glitters is gold. Something shiny may be worth little. The writer means a flashy label may not mean a good product.
